7 October 2026 · for the founding team · reviewed by Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Sol

Running a Job

Why designers get lost in The Document, and three ways to show them the way.

Five tasks every reviewer walked

  1. A new inquiry arrives. What do I do first, and how do I know?
  2. The client asks for a change after signing. Where do I record it?
  3. “Where is the PO for the sofa?” Find it, and what is blocking it.
  4. It’s install week. What’s late, what’s arriving, what do I do?
  5. A new hire opens someone else’s job cold. What stage, whose move, what next?

Scenarios from BRIEF.md. Evidence is code on main plus a local seeded walk. Nothing here touched production.

02 / 24
The ask

Designers are getting lost and don’t know what to do.

Kody, the ask behind this review

Who is lost: the first hire, opening a job someone else wrote

VISION §2 names the studio moment: a growing studio adding its first hands while the workload doubles. “The thing she cannot afford is a new system to learn.” Leah fills the gaps from memory. Her first hire didn’t write the job she opens. She opens a paper cold, from a link or the Desk, and has to tell from the page alone what stage it is in, whose move it is, and what to do next. That is the reader this review was written for.

Leah
Founder-designer. Deep domain expertise, little patience for software.
The hire
A junior designer or design assistant. Competent in the craft, new to the studio’s way and to Patina, often working someone else’s job.
Scope
Running a job in The Document (/doc/[id]), from inquiry to care.
Not here
No product code, migrations, flags, Sanity or production. Review and design only.

Sources: BRIEF.md (the ask, personas, canon) · docs/vision/VISION.md §2.

03 / 24
Thesis

August made the Document quiet for the person who wrote the job. The studio is now adding people who didn’t write it.

The Document can calculate the next step at every stage. It just doesn’t say it in one voice, in words, where a designer looks. Six devices each answer part of “what now?”, each in its own words.

“What now?”

  1. The lens band

    “File the claim”

    For the same damage claim, the Desk says “Review the claim”. The guide and the Desk differ on six need kinds, by design.

    document-guide.ts:596-635 · desk-derivation.ts:160-189
  2. The spine

    “ACTIVE”

    The rail prints a status word: ACTIVE, ONGOING or INSTALLATION. It never prints the stage.

    A1 · walk/s5-step1-olsen-opened.jpg
  3. The letterhead

    “No client linked — attach one”

    Its loudest line outweighs the title. The stage is an unlabelled mark under the client’s name.

    A1 · A6 · walk/project-1440.jpg
  4. The region heads

    “Continue drafting”

    On the same Direction paper the band says “Open the Contract Room”. One door, four labels on one screen.

    proposal-instruments.tsx:397 · document-guide.ts:169
  5. The margin

    “VENDOR PAYMENT DUE”

    On Chen Residence, while the band reads “Balance to Woodward & Sons” for the same money.

    walk/project-1440.jpg · specimens/SPEC.md §4
  6. ⌘K

    “Open the Contract Room”

    Here it continues a draft. The same words on the Desk create a new one.

    command-bar.tsx:879 · desk-contents.tsx:407

The one device built to answer, the band, has room for one sentence. On any live job something is late, so that sentence goes to the late thing and the stage’s next step prints nowhere. Leah fills the gaps from memory. A first hire, opening someone else’s job, can’t.

Sources: synthesis/direction.md §1 · briefing/current-state.md §2, contradictions 4, 5 and 9 of 13 · walk/WALK.md.

04 / 24
August

We tried this in August

  1. 25 Aug

    The wayfinding review: nine reviewers, 92 findings. Two directions: A “Everything Prints” and B “The Shop Ticket”, the job ticket. R124

  2. 26 Aug

    R124 and R125 built both, with no flags. The job ticket shipped. I146–I151

  3. 28 Aug

    The Smart Lens proposal: one 56px band printing the worst standing thing, with +N MORE for the rest. R127

  4. 29–30 Aug

    The lens band replaced the ticket. The job ticket was deleted four days after it shipped, before anyone compared it with the band. 48d5b0de5

Why it didn’t land

Every acceptance gate in R127 was geometric: band height, CLS, first-head position, blank frames. No gate asked a person to finish a task: find the next act, record a change, find a PO.

The one structural answer, Direction B’s job ticket, was gone before anyone set it beside the band.

August measured whether the devices printed correctly. Nobody tested whether a designer could finish a task with them.

R1 · Opus 5.5

August made the Document quieter. It did not make it legible to someone who was not there yesterday.

R2 · Fable 5.1

1 · A new inquiry Found immediatelyThe Desk. She knows who Chen and Aspen are. The Desk prose reads as the whole worklist. Nothing on the page points to the 7 more or to ⌘K.

The change order lives inside a line’s unfold. 1 click on the Pieces rail landed on the Schedule; no confident path past it One wrong stop, then Pieces from memory. She shrugs it off. 09 / 24
Reviewers

Where they split, and what we took from each

The next act’s slot

R1 rates it S1: blocking items and the next step share line 2, so the next step disappears on busy jobs (R1-01). R2 sees the right rhythm for Leah and the wrong one for a cold reader. R3 asks for a reason line rather than another slot.

Taken: split the band into Next and Standing (Direction A). The cold-reader fix sits on top of that (Direction B).

R126, Ink on Paper

R1 argues it flattened act weight: primary and tertiary look alike, and the flooded tier went to region leaders. R2 keeps R126’s register as “simply right”. R3 says flatness isn’t the cause, so fix wording first.

Taken: keep the register and change who gets the weight. Only the next act is heavy; the filled tier is for money or signature. This is V9 applied, not R126 reversed.

Install

R1 and R2 say R124 item 3 (“install stays a label”) can stand: the fix is a lateness need kind plus the leader rule. R3 frames it as a founder question.

Taken: no mode. The Install region leads with a dated reading. R3’s question is kept, and the answer is “no ruling needed”.

Whose move

Only R2 names it. Discovery’s “Yours to add: scope. Waiting on the Ashfords: budget and 3 more” is the only ownership sentence in the product, and the Desk card’s YOUR PEN never reaches the paper.

Taken: this becomes Direction B, the clearest link between this review and the studio moment.

Unique catches worth carrying

  • The red-letter zone is no longer mounted at all, so the brief’s map was stale. R1-14
  • A held job looks live. R1-22
  • The phone dock’s centre is “Message the client” on every stage, even with no client linked. R1-11 · R2-08 · F52 unchanged
  • The money acts (bill, release, send) are the quietest on the page, and their refusals don’t say why. R2-32 · R1-39
  • “$0 proposed” should read “Not priced yet”. R3-21

Source: synthesis/direction.md §3.

These are layers, not rivals.

All three keep the canon that holds: one Document (V7 D1, no tabs), NG1 (no persistent global nav), NG2 (the shadow budget), V11’s ledger test, R126’s register and V12’s arrival. None adds a dashboard, a task manager or a badge. Each passes the VISION feature test.

The remedy is not another place to manage work.

11 / 24 Direction A · One Voice

A · One Voice: the next act, said once, in one name

  • One label table. Every device that prints a next act reads it: band, Desk card, ⌘K, region head, dock. The act’s name is the name of the control it lands on, and the press lands with focus on that control.
  • The band gets two fixed positions: Next ─ <act> on the left, Standing · <worst> +N on the right. Silence on the right when nothing stands.
  • The stage in words in the letterhead eyebrow: PROJECT · 5 OF 7, using the seven document words only.
  • Weight by role. Only the Next act and its twin at the head of the active region are heavy. The filled tier stays for money or signature. A gated act prints its reason under it.

Acceptance

How we’ll know: a person finishes the five tasks

Acceptance for every slice is the five scenarios, walked by a person who did not build the job, at 1440 and 390, with the step count recorded. That replaces geometry-only gates. Today’s walk is the baseline.

  1. A new inquiry arrives. Today: found on the Desk at 0 clicks; the third lead needs one more.
  2. A change after signing. Today: not found. One click landed on the Schedule.
  3. The PO for the sofa. Today: one failed search, two clicks, still one tab from the PO.
  4. Install week. Today: one click to the Install region; nothing says late or arriving.
  5. A cold open. Today: 0 clicks to two needs at equal weight; no stage word.
Who walks
Someone who didn’t build the job. Leah’s first hire, or whoever is closest to that.
Where
1440 and 390.
Record
The step count for each scenario.
Replaces
Geometry-only gates, like R127’s band height, CLS, first-head position and blank frames.

21 / 24
Questions

Eight questions for the founders

Each needs a ruling before its slice ships. The numbers are real: the rest of the work refers to them as Q1 to Q8.

  1. Q1

    The stage word · R127 L-6

    Should the stage print in words at the top of every paper? Yield the count, never the word. All three reviewers ask for this.

    If noA cold reader still can’t tell the stage from the paper (A1, scenario 5).

  2. Q2

    Next and Standing · R127 OD-11 / L-11

    May the band carry the next act and the worst standing item side by side, instead of making them share one slot?

    If noOn any live job the next step keeps losing its one slot to the late thing (R1-01).

  3. Q3

    Ranking by kind · R127 W3-R1

    Keep deadline order within a class, but put “blocks money or a signature” ahead of everything else. Setup is never painted as an exception.

    If noA setup chore and a damage claim keep competing on one scale, and install week keeps leading with a chore (A4).

  4. Q4

    The stage vocabulary · R124 item 7 / I114

    Should only the seven document words ever print as stage on a studio surface, with the eleven-stage workflow names kept in data?

    If noOne stage keeps printing under several names, and an open gate swaps in the other vocabulary (R1-03, contradiction 13).

  5. Q5

    “Absence is silence” · V9 §5

    Is a missing expected act a named sentence rather than silence (for example “Only the owner can close the book”, “Held since 2 Oct”)?

    If noA held job stays silent and a non-owner sees no control and no reason (R1-22, R1-23).

  6. Q6

    The first open · R127 L-11

    May a paper show its full standing list once, the first time a person opens it?

    If noThe first hire meets one line and a +N MORE door with no kind and no order (A10).

  7. Q7

    VISION §4, read for the first hire

    Add one sentence: the paper says where it is and whose move it is before she asks.

    If noDirection B has no canon to stand on, and the Document stays tuned for its author (R2 §2).

  8. Q8

    Process

    Make the five scenarios, walked by someone who didn’t build the job, the acceptance gate for wayfinding work.

    If noThe next program can pass every gate again without anyone finishing a task, as August did.

Source: synthesis/direction.md §6. The cost lines draw on §2, §3 and the review findings cited.
